video_title: How Spark Dodged the KelpDAO Hack While the Rest of DeFi Got Hit
gist: Sam MacPherson, co-founder and CEO of Spark (a Sky/MakerDAO sub-DAO run operationally by Phoenix Labs), explains the specific design choices — rate limits on lending markets, no ETH looping/e-mode for newer collateral, a triple-redundant oracle, and a January off-boarding of rETH — that left Spark unscathed by the KelpDAO exploit while the rest of DeFi took losses, with Spark's ETH TVL up ~50% since mid-April. He also lays out Sky's sub-DAO 'central bank / commercial bank' structure, argues stablecoin yields compress toward SOFR because of excess idle stablecoin liquidity, frames the current hack wave as opsec rather than smart-contract failure that AI plus formal verification will ultimately fix, and defends the SPK token on DCF/buyback grounds despite it trading at or near all-time lows.

themes.theme: Sky sub-DAO architecture and Spark's balance sheet

insights.claim: Sky (formerly MakerDAO) has restructured into a model where Sky acts as a central bank and wholesale liquidity issuer while sub-DAOs such as Spark act as commercial banks drawing on Sky's reserves to make loans.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: The central-bank/commercial-bank split is the template other large DAOs may copy; it determines where revenue and risk actually sit when underwriting SPK versus SKY.
insights.quote: Sky functions um more like a central bank and wholesale uh liquidity issuer. So, the sub DAOs, Spark being one of these, is functions more as a commercial bank

insights.claim: Spark Savings is an allocator vault sitting on top of USDC and USDT that routes depositor capital across DeFi, CeFi and TradFi RWAs, quoted at 3.6% on USDC and 2.75% on USDT at the time of recording in mid-July.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A concrete benchmark for 'conservative' on-chain stablecoin yield to compare against the 7%+ promotional rates being offered by neobanks and exchanges.

insights.claim: Spark Prime is an early-stage CeFi prime brokerage letting hedge funds cross-margin positions across DeFi, CeFi and now TradFi venues, explicitly aimed at the tokenized-stocks hype cycle and connecting it to venues like Hyperliquid.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Cross-venue margin is the missing plumbing for basis and stock-vs-perp trades; whoever wins it captures financing spread across the whole stack.

themes.theme: Why Spark survived the KelpDAO exploit

insights.claim: Spark's ETH-denominated TVL is up roughly 50% from mid-April and was up about 80% in early July, making it a direct beneficiary of the KelpDAO hack that damaged the rest of DeFi.
insights.speaker: host, Laura Shin
insights.so_what: Security incidents are a share-shifting event in DeFi lending; conservative protocols capture deposits that flee compromised venues.
insights.quote: The TVL in ETH is up about 50% from that time today and even in early July it was up about 80% from that point.

insights.claim: Spark has capped withdrawal throughput with rate limits on every market since shortly after its 2023 launch and never supported the looping strategies rival markets ran, on the logic that attackers must convert stolen collateral into ETH or BTC immediately while legitimate borrowers tolerate waiting.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A reusable mental model for evaluating any on-chain venue: how much value can leave per unit time, and does urgency correlate with fraud.
insights.quote: The ones who need to go through right away, uh usually there's something wrong there.

insights.claim: The KelpDAO exploit required two conditions — an asset-issuer configuration mistake (the LayerZero setup) plus a deep exit venue, with Aave named as the main venue used to convert into ETH.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Exploit losses concentrate in whichever lending market offers the deepest instant exit, so venue depth is itself a liability in a hack.
insights.quote: you kind of need the asset issuer to um make a mistake with uh you know, the way the layer zero configuration was with with KelpDAO. You need and then you needed a venue to get to to ETH. And so, Aave was uh the main venue for this.

insights.claim: Spark runs a triple-redundant oracle across Chainlink, Redstone and Chronicle so the market stays live even if one provider prints a bad price.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Oracle redundancy is a cheap, checkable differentiator between lending protocols and a direct hedge against manipulation-style attacks.
insights.quote: we run uh a triple-redundant Oracle. So, even if one of the major providers, so we run it between Chainlink, Redstone, and Chronicle.

insights.claim: Spark had off-boarded rETH in January as part of routine risk reduction, and even if it had not, the asset was never enabled in high-leverage efficiency mode and carried only 60-70% LTVs for stablecoin borrowing, so losses would likely have been minimal or recoverable.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Collateral tiering — which assets get e-mode versus stablecoin-only borrowing — is where lending-market losses are actually decided.

insights.claim: Spark Lend has deliberately shrunk to roughly five collateral assets — cbBTC, wBTC, Lido staked ETH and EtherFi — on the view that a minimal collateral set covers nearly all organic usage while eliminating tail risk.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Collateral-list length is a proxy for tail risk in lending markets; expanding lists during bull markets is the leading indicator of the next blowup.

insights.claim: Spark's normal governance process takes about a month, running through a risk council of three reviewing teams, an SPK snapshot vote, and a final check by Sky against its risk framework.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A one-month change latency means routine de-risking must be anticipatory, not reactive — a structural constraint when evaluating protocol agility.
insights.quote: the governance process takes on on the order of about a month

insights.claim: Holding assets under custody with no time lock makes a protocol a direct target for North Korean attackers, which MacPherson cites the Drift hack as evidence of.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Time-lock presence is a binary screen for custody risk in DeFi protocols; its absence is an active attractant for state-level attackers.
insights.quote: Having assets under custody with no time lock is actually uh quite dangerous and makes you a target for North Korea, as as we can see with like the Drift hack, for example.

insights.claim: Flat DAO governance failed at Maker because political factions and informal alliances formed with no natural structure to hold them, which is why the sub-DAO model was designed to let the core DAO set only rules and risk policy while sub-DAOs compete to deliver value.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A concrete alternative to the current wave of DAOs disbanding or recentralizing; if sub-DAOs work, expect other large protocols to fragment the same way.
insights.quote: we do this quickly realize this like flat structure just doesn't work

insights.claim: Phoenix Labs is run as an operating company that raises no money of its own so that all value accrues to the SPK token rather than to private equity.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Token-versus-equity value accrual is the central question for DeFi token holders; a labs entity with no raise removes the usual dilution overhang.
insights.quote: we are not raising money under Phoenix Labs or anything like that

themes.theme: AI-driven hacks and the formal-verification endgame

insights.claim: DeFi is at a peak danger zone from AI-enabled attacks but will end up safer because AI is equally usable defensively, with formal verification as the destination.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Implies the current hack wave is a temporary drawdown in DeFi TVL rather than a structural end-state — a contrarian buy-the-fear framing.
insights.quote: right now we are probably in like a a peak sort of danger zone, but I I feel like we're going to move actually to a better place ultimately because AI, although it can be used on the offensive, it can also be used on the defensive

insights.claim: The major recent crypto hacks are opsec failures rather than smart-contract failures, because modern smart contracts are intentionally minimal while the compromised systems are millions of lines of conventional software.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Redirects diligence away from contract audits toward operational security and key management — the actual attack surface being exploited.
insights.quote: If you look at the major hacks, these are all opsec hacks and opsec like again, we know how to do this correctly.

insights.claim: Phoenix Labs is already using AI alongside human auditors internally and reports that AI is starting to catch up to the best available human auditors.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A near-term threat to the crypto audit services business model and a cost deflator for protocol security budgets.
insights.quote: It is starting to become good enough that it is actually um catching up to some of the the best human auditors that are available.

themes.theme: Stablecoin yield compression and distribution wars

insights.claim: On-chain stablecoin yields converge toward SOFR because there is an excess of stablecoin liquidity searching for yield, not because the risk is genuinely low — Sky holds around 10 billion with only about 40% deployed into lending and much sitting idle.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Explains why DeFi lending rates stay near T-bill levels despite elevated hack risk; the supply glut, not risk pricing, sets the rate.
insights.quote: there is just an excess of uh stablecoin liquidity searching for yield and in the space. So, um this is naturally leads to more compressed rates.

insights.claim: The Coinbase playbook of pairing a distribution channel with an owned chain and an owned stablecoin is being copied by Robinhood and by Stripe with Tempo, because each wants to own the net interest margin on its own stablecoin.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Identifies the repeating distribution-plus-chain-plus-stablecoin pattern as the competitive template; the NIM prize is what to model when valuing these issuers.
insights.quote: everybody wants to own the uh own the net interest margin that comes from having users using their stablecoin um within the DeFi ecosystem

insights.claim: Spark was selected as one of three asset issuers backing Robinhood's 7% USDG earn product, positioning it as the yield supplier to competing distribution front-ends rather than a competitor for retail deposits.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Picks-and-shovels positioning: Spark earns from the stablecoin distribution war regardless of which front-end wins.

insights.claim: Sky is one of the largest on-chain holders of USDC and can therefore market-make new stablecoins like USDG at effectively zero cost of capital because the inventory is idle anyway, letting upstart issuers scale without bank rails or redemption fees.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Idle stablecoin inventory is a monetizable moat; this is a structural advantage traditional market makers with funding costs cannot match.

insights.claim: Spark launched a stablecoin FX layer with Uniswap intended to create the 'singleness of money' for stablecoins — the interchangeability that the Fed provides for bank deposits but which does not exist in DeFi.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: If one protocol becomes the clearing layer between competing stablecoins, it captures a toll on the entire multi-issuer stablecoin economy.
insights.quote: it really helps improve sort of uh what you call like the singleness of money where in the traditional banking system, the Fed backs all the US dollar deposits into banks and so bank deposits they're largely interchangeable

themes.theme: SPK token valuation and growth pipeline

insights.claim: MacPherson expects crypto token consolidation where only a few store-of-value assets like Bitcoin, ETH and SOL survive on narrative, while equity-like tokens converge on DCF valuation.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A concrete screen for altcoin allocation: separate monetary assets from cash-flow assets and underwrite the latter on revenue, not narrative.
insights.quote: the rest of the tokens I think are just going to converge on like a a DCF valuation

insights.claim: Spark publishes protocol financials on data.spark.fi with quarterly reports and has governance-approved buybacks funded from excess profits, which MacPherson uses to justify not worrying about SPK trading at or near all-time lows.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Disclosed financials plus a buyback mandate make SPK one of the few tokens actually testable against the DCF thesis he describes.
insights.quote: excess profits will go to buybacks in in the token

insights.claim: Spark's institutional lending business, launched at the end of last year, has reached 250 million in loans issued and is targeted to reach a billion and beyond by the end of the year on a stated robust pipeline.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: A trackable, near-term revenue growth metric — a 4x target on a disclosed base makes the DCF case falsifiable within two quarters.
insights.quote: We are up to 250 million in loans issued there and we're on track. We have a robust pipeline that is on track to grow to I think a billion and beyond by the end of the year.

insights.claim: Spark aims to be positioned as the conservative place to park cash on chain, competing on safety and disclosure rather than on headline yield against 7%-plus offers from exchange and neobank rivals.
insights.speaker: Sam MacPherson
insights.so_what: Defines the competitive lane: if the hack wave persists, safety-first positioning wins deposit share even at a several-hundred-basis-point yield discount.
insights.quote: we're we're aiming for Spark to be sort of like the conservative version of this where you can just park your cash and not have to worry about it
